newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Di Pietro says there is no going back.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Di Pietro says there is no going back.

text.p: The symbol of Italy's "Clean Hands" anti-graft team, ex-magistrate Antonio di Pietro, has said he will fight to clear its name and will not go back on his decision to resign as public works minister.

In an open letter to Prime Minister Romano Prodi published in newspapers on Monday, the former prosecutor said people were attacking him to undermine the elite pool of Clean Hands magistrates in Milan.
"I have to stop it," he said in his brief letter.

Di Pietro stormed out of the government last week after coming under investigation for alleged malpractice during his time with the team in the early 1990s, when its investigations into corruption toppled Italy's governing class.
"I have understood the "monstrosity' of what they are trying to do, using me against the validity of the Clean Hands enquiries," Di Pietro wrote.

Di Pietro quit the Milan magistrature in December 1994 amid rumours that he had been forced out. He emerged with his reputation intact earlier this year from allegations of abuse of office that were thrown out of court.
The latest investigation derives from a probe being led by prosecutors in the northern port city of La Spezia.
The case revolves around an international banker, Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia, who was investigated by Di Pietro in 1993 for his alleged role in a massive bribes scandal.
Charges were pressed but Pacini Battaglia was not held in preventative detention, unlike many other suspects.
In a telephone tap, leaked to the press, Pacini Battaglia hinted that he had paid a bribe to avoid prison.

Di Pietro has vehemently denied any wrongdoing and Prodi has expressed full confidence in him. The Italian cabinet on Saturday called on Di Pietro, who belongs to no political party, to return to the six-month-old government.

"I want to thank all the ministers for their solidarity," Di Pietro wrote in his letter to Prodi, but he said that his decision was irreversible. "Believe me, this action shows no disrespect to yourself or to the government," he added.
